question: The average height of 15 boys out of a class of 50 is 160 cm. If the average height of the remaining boys is 168 cm, the average height (in cm) of all the boys of the class is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of boys = 15 : 35 → **3 : 7**

Assume average height = **160 cm**

Deviation in second group = 168 − 160 = **+8 cm**

Net deviation for total parts (10) = 7 × 8 = **+56**

Average height = 160 + (56 ÷ 10) = 160 + 5.6 = **165.6 cm**

**∴ The correct answer is 165.6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of boys in first group (n₁) = **15**

Average height of first group (A₁) = **160 cm**

Total number of boys (N) = **50**

Average height of remaining boys (A₂) = **168 cm**

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a80e76dcb3a24a494b805d277a6f6b2db25ccb5a37704757b75b628281125eec.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total height of first 15 boys = 15 × 160 = **2400 cm**

⇒ Number of remaining boys = 50 − 15 = **35 boys**

⇒ Total height of 35 boys = 35 × 168 = **5880 cm**

⇒ Total height of all 50 boys = 2400 + 5880 = **8280 cm**

⇒ Average height of class = 8280 ÷ 50

⇒ Average height = **165.6 cm**

**∴ The correct answer is 165.6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Concept

When groups with different averages are combined, the combined average is the total sum divided by the total count: Aₐvg = Σ (nᵢ × Aᵢ) ÷ Σ nᵢ.

Deviation Method (Change in Average)

If one group is considered as the base average, the overall average increases/decreases by the (net deviation) ÷ (total quantity).

Alligation Rule

The ratio of the quantities is inversely proportional to the differences between their averages and the mean average: n₁/n₂ = (A₂ − Aₘₑₐₙ) / (Aₘₑₐₙ − A₁).</p
